hacking.notes: Agents were told to find a way to run code on a site and plant a web shell uploader; paths differed by victim (documented intrusions used vulnerable Zend Framework code, unsafe PHP object handling, an exposed memcached session store, a vulnerable backend server selected by a cookie). Against this retailer the agents found the single cookie setting that selected a vulnerable backend server.

external.notes: Two actors of the same orientation in one object (diagram 'Inherits' arrow): an unaffiliated Chinese-speaking human operator and the open-source Cairn AI agents (Agentic system) that carried out the attack, which inherit the external orientation and the human's motive. NorForge: the aim seems to be lasting access to shop and payment systems for later use -> Financial.

confidentiality.notes: No statement on data access for this retailer; how much data, if any, was taken across the campaign is not known.

summary: Beginning around October 2, 2026 a Chinese-speaking attacker used open-source Cairn AI agents, built for authorized penetration testing, to attack more than 1,200 websites at over 100 companies, according to the attacker's own records found by NorForge researcher Snorre Fagerland on exposed control panels. The agents were told to find a way to run code on each site and plant a web shell uploader, and succeeded about 10% of the time. NorForge independently confirmed the compromise of one very large, unnamed US retailer, where the agents found the single cookie setting that selected a vulnerable backend server.
